input.question: Why does a hearing a recording of my voice sound different to me then when I hear myself talk?
input.ground_truth: We hear sounds as vibrations hitting our ear drums. When we hear most sounds, these vibrations travel through the air and into the ear canal. Our own voices also vibrate through our bodies, creating a slightly lower pitch. When you hear a recording of your voice you are missing this extra level of vibration that lowers the sound, so your voice sounds higher than what you are used to. Source: _URL_0_

Question: Why does a hearing a recording of my voice sound different to me then when I hear myself talk?

Answer:

response.prediction: When you hear a recording of your voice, it sounds different from how you hear yourself talk because of the way sound travels. When you speak, some of the sound vibrations travel through your bones and skull directly to your inner ear. This makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself. However, when you hear a recording, the sound reaches your ears only through the air, just like how you hear other people's voices. This version of your voice usually sounds higher and thinner to you because it lacks the bone-conducted vibrations. That’s why your recorded voice can sound unfamiliar, even though it is actually how others hear you.
